title: Exec weekly pulse scratchpad
content:
Monday 2026-03-09 -> Friday 2026-03-13

Top-of-day quick list (start here each morning):
- 08:30: review latency dashboard (p50/p95), note any regressions
- 09:00: 1:1 with Marcus (SRE) — discuss incident RCA progress and runbook gaps
- 10:00: Hosted API metrics sync (ops)
- 11:00: Sales demo prep for ACME (Dedicated contract) — finalize pricing slide and fallbacks

Weekly goals (stretch):
1) Finalize Dedicated capacity SLAs wording for Enterprise contracts
   - draft to Legal by Tue EOD (owner: Aisha)
   - get Legal review Wed, Exec sign-off Thu
2) Ship two quick Optimize recommendations in console (batching + kv cache defaults)
   - PRs ready Wed (owner: engineering: Claire)
3) Reduce p95 latency by 10% on small prompt class via kernel selection tweak
   - SLO experiment runs Tue-Fri (owner: serving-runtime)

Meeting prep notes:
- 1:1 with Marcus: ask for timeline on incident action items; confirm retest date; confirm on-call rotation changes
- Product review (Wed 14:00): bring concrete rollout plan for model variant routing (A/B + canary); show e2e failure mode
- ACME contract call (Thu 11:30): have fallback models list, dedicated capacity commitment tiers, and SOC2 on hand

Action items & follow-ups (tracked quick):
- [ ] Draft Dedicated SLA language — due 2026-03-10 — owner: Aisha
- [ ] Ping Claire for Optimize PR status — due 2026-03-11 — owner: Aisha
- [ ] Add canary rollback checklist to repo (link in linked_artifacts) — due 2026-03-12 — owner: Release Eng
- [ ] Confirm on-call rota proposal with SRE — due 2026-03-13 — owner: Marcus
- [ ] Add metric alert for kv cache hit-rate drop — due 2026-03-12 — owner: Observability

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep customer-facing demo simple: show latency, cost delta, and failover story
- If legal pushes back on 'auto-fallback' wording, propose 'automatic model substitution' with audit logs
- Consider weekly 'cost anomaly' email digest for top 10 teams
- Remind PMs to include prompt-suite for quality monitoring (small sampling first)

Open questions:
- How aggressive do we want default batching? latency SLO vs unit-cost tradeoff — need product decision Thurs.
- Capacity pricing tiers: should we bake in a buffer for burst (10% vs 20%)?
- Are there PII concerns in customer's kv cache keys? check with security.

Bottom-of-day quick log (fill before sign-off):
- 17:45: Quick diary: what shipped, blocked items, next-day focus

Random links I keep handy:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RW-ops-weekly
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RW-4123
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/278

Small wins this week:
- Observability now surfaces token-level cost per route (early beta)
- Can run golden prompt evals nightly (first pass done)

Tone notes: keep bullets terse, escalate blockers asap, maintain 'customer-first but pragmatic' framing in discussions.

Quick end-of-week retro bullets (Fri):
- What worked: faster cross-team sync on incidents
- What didn't: contract language took longer than expected
- Next week focus: streamline SLA wording process, product decision on batching defaults
